channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Trump says what Russia is doing to Ukraine is 'fine'
item.description: Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bill Taylor reacts to the latest comments from President Donald Trump on Russia as questions grow over America's support of Ukraine.

item.title: Woman killed in shark attack in South Africa
item.description: A 65-year-old woman was killed in a shark attack at a popular beach on South Africa's southeastern coast, local authorities said.

item.title: Couple charged in fatal shooting of 17-year-old on her way to zoo
item.description: A husband and wife from Texas have been arrested and charged in the killing of a 17-year-old who was shot on Interstate 170 last week.

item.title: Trump attacks Democratic challenger Hamilton at Kansas rally as Senate race tightens
item.description: President Donald Trump took the stage in Kansas on Monday night to campaign for Sen. Roger Marshall, a one-term incumbent facing a close race against Adam Hamilton.

item.title: Controversial Jackdaw gas field expected to be approved
item.description: The controversial Jackdaw gas field is expected to receive approval from energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh on Wednesday.

item.title: US nearing deal with Russia to free multiple jailed Americans: Sources
item.description: Sources say the talks have centered on freeing Stephen Hubbard.

item.title: How French police are harnessing social media to identify looters
item.description: French police are turning to social media to identify and arrest suspects linked to last weekend’s looting and unrest. Investigators are scrutinising videos posted online alongside footage from thousands of security cameras to track suspects and gather evidence. The crackdown comes as the government vows to hold those responsible for the violence and damage to shops accountable.

item.title: Man arrested for alleged threats to shoot President Trump at Kansas rally
item.description: Authorities allege the man posted several threatening messages on Facebook.

item.title: Vanessa Kerry is the new WHO envoy for health resilience. What's on her to-do list?
item.description: A respected figure in the world of global health, Dr. Kerry takes on a new responsibility. She says it's challenging but not "daunting."

item.title: More than 150 killed in Sudan drone strike on disputed Abyei border region
item.description: At least 153 people have been killed in a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region, where a fire at a nearby fuel depot continued to burn on Tuesday. Local officials blamed Sudan’s military for Monday’s attack, which also left dozens injured.

item.title: France: Local curfews imposed after protests
item.description: French cities that imposed a curfew Monday saw a generally calm night, after October 17 protests devolved into violent riots this past weekend. Despite criticism from citizens, France's government said it is maintaining the measure where necessary on Tuesday night.

item.title: DOJ charges 28 with unlawful voting, other election-related offenses in California
item.description: The DOJ has charged 28 individuals in California with election-related offenses, and did not rule out prosecuting election workers who are "processing the ballots" there.

item.title: France's decades-long ties with Gulf states built on 'economic development, oil, defence agreements'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome François Gouyette, former French ambassador to the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Against a backdrop of violent unrest at home and escalating conflict in the Middle East, French President Emmanuel Macron's Gulf diplomacy underscores the increasingly blurred boundaries between domestic economic security and international strategic commitments. Ambassador Gouyette argues that the visit serves a dual purpose: alleviating France's energy pressures while reaffirming its longstanding defense partnerships with Gulf monarchies. Insisting that "France has to play its role as a key partner," Gouyette portrays French military assistance as an expression of strategic solidarity rather than direct participation in the war with Iran.

item.title: US midterm elections: Trump approval rating falls to new low
item.description: With US President Donald Trump’s approval rating falling to a record low of 31%, Republicans are facing mounting concerns ahead of November’s midterm elections. Republicans are at risk of losing control of the House of Representatives, but how big could the Democrats’ gains be? FRANCE 24’s International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: Two men re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran after RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Two men have been re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service over a suspected terror plot near RAF Fairford.

item.title: From fine wine to no alcohol: The changing world of French sommeliers
item.description: In this week's edition of France in Focus, our reporters uncork the demanding world of sommellerie. They follow Pascaline Lepeltier's painstaking training as she prepares for the World's Best Sommelier competition. They also explore how the profession is adapting to changing drinking habits, meeting one sommelier who's chosen to go alcohol-free.

item.title: French PM vows 'massive' police deployment for new demonstrations Saturday
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Tuesday authorities would mobilise a "massive" security presence next weekend, with organisers announcing plans for new protests after riots erupted on the sidelines of nationwide demonstrations. "The deployment for next Saturday will be massive," Lecornu said in parliament, acknowledging that the security operation for the protests last weekend had been "too static and not mobile enough." FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago reports from Place de la République in central Paris.

item.title: October 17 riots in France: Who's responsible?
item.description: We take a look at who is responsible for the violence that broke out in France on October 17. We dive into who the casseurs, or lawbreakers, are and how a bill is proposing that they pay for the damage they caused. We also discuss the French government’s mea culpa and the ongoing political blame game, with a budding controversy over whether the vandals were "ultra-left" members or not.

item.title: Some older siblings left raising family members after parents' deportation: Advocates
item.description: Some older siblings have been left to care for their younger family members following the deportation of their parents, advocacy groups say.

item.title: French Justice Minister promises 'extremely firm' punishment for rioters
item.description: This ​weekend's rioting ​in France highlighted failings in the security ​services' ‌handling of ‌threats posed by looters, said Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin. He promised that rioters would face extremely firm punishment. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley tells us more.

item.title: French PM blames 'ultra-left' groups for weekend riots, promises 'massive' security deployment
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said Tuesday during a session of the National Assembly that authorities would mobilise a "massive" security presence next weekend after organisers announced plans for new protests. Lecornu also accused ultra-left groups of fomenting an "insurrection" leading to the past weekend's riots on the sidelines of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living and education funding.

item.title: Ukraine ‘losing people and time’, Zelensky says after Oslo talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has wrapped up talks with US envoys in Norway Tuesday where he was determined to put diplomacy back on a "more constructive path”, Oslo officials said. Zelensky told a post-meeting press briefing that Ukraine was not losing the war but was “losing people and time” saying he was hopeful moving forward because “we have some clear ideas of how to get peace”.

item.title: Midterms: Trump seizes on unrest in France for political gain
item.description: Donald #Trump seizes on unrest in #France to attack immigration and the #Democrats, using the issue as a campaign message ahead of the November 3 US #midterms.

item.title: Alberta rejects move toward independence from Canada
item.description: Canada's province of Alberta rejected a plan to hold a binding independence referendum, results showed Tuesday, a win for unity as the country faces worsening ties with the United States. With more than 1.5 million votes counted, 76% supported remaining in Canada, while close to 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.

item.title: Macron secures 200,000 tonnes of extra diesel per month from UAE, Bahrain
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has secured the delivery of an additional 200,000 tonnes of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, the French presidency said on Tuesday. Macron is undertaking a tour of key energy suppliers in the Gulf in an effort to secure oil and diesel and bring down prices in France, after a weekend of violent protests over soaring living costs. FRANCE 24'S Tarek Kaï reports from Doha, Qatar.

item.title: France unrest: Public reacts to PM’s announcement of new targeted curfews
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has announced that new targeted curfews would be put in place this Tuesday in France. This comes after measures introduced overnight helped maintain calm following unrest over the weekend.

item.title: Norwegian explorer Erling Kagge: 'The Arctic is heating up in every way'
item.description: In Perspective, we spoke to the Norwegian explorer Erling Kagge, the first man to reach the North Pole unassisted by animals or vehicles. He is also the first person ever to reach the North and South Poles and the summit of Mount Everest on foot. His book "The North Pole: The History of an Obsession" has just come out in French translation.

item.title: France's sociopolitical & economic crises: 'Large portion of population sympathizes' with protestors
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Damien Lecomte, Political Scientist and Researcher at Paris Panthéon Sorbonne University. France’s escalating unrest has exposed a profound contradiction in the state’s response: disproportionate force against peaceful demonstrators and an inability to contain widespread violence. As competing narratives threaten to overshadow legitimate grievances over education, public services and the cost of living, he warns that the "repressive response won't make the social crisis disappear.” With presidential elections approaching, the struggle to restore order is becoming inseparable from a deeper contest over political legitimacy, public liberties and the future direction of French society.

item.title: Suspect arrested in France after fire at historic city hall
item.description: A man has been arrested after a fire at the town hall of Limoges, according to French media.

item.title: Rubio and Jaishankar hold talks in Mumbai as US and India aim to finalize trade deal
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has held talks with India's foreign minister in Mumbai

item.title: Six years on, France remembers slain teacher Samuel Paty
item.description: French schoolteacher Samuel Paty was killed on October 16, 2020 after false rumours circulated about racism following one of his lessons in which cartoons from the satirical publication Charlie Hebdo were shown. For the first time since his murder, journalists from France Télévisions were allowed to film inside the school where he taught in Conflans-Sainte-Honorine, near Paris. They met a new generation of young people, who are determined to play their part in the fight against terrorism.

item.title: Ivorian DJ digs forgotten tracks, on the hunt for great classics
item.description: Cédric Kouamé travels across Ivory Coast to collect old vinyl records before restoring them. The Ivorian DJ hopes to bring national attention to his passion through an official centre dedicated to the country's historical archives, as FRANCE 24's team on the ground reports.

item.title: Midterms 2026: The farmers calling for more migrant workers
item.description: As the US midterms approach, immigration is once again dominating the country’s political discourse and Arizona’s largely agricultural Yuma County, just miles from the Mexican border, is no exception. But here, farmers like John Boelts are calling for more legal migrants, warning that without the labour they provide essential crops may go to waste or never be planted at all. France 24’s Sam Ball and Barbara Gabel sent this report.

item.title: ‘I don't recognise the country I grew up in anymore’: Some Israelis tempted by exile
item.description: From our special correspondent in Tel Aviv – Since 2023, Israel has experienced an unprecedented brain drain. With the October 27 legislative elections approaching, many graduates are considering leaving the country if the right-wing and far-right coalition led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remains in power.

item.title: Channels to close as BBC announces details of cuts
item.description: The BBC has confirmed it will close BBC Three, BBC Scotland and BBC Radio 4 Extra linear broadcast services in the spring of 2027.

item.title: Neglect in hospital contributed to baby's meningitis death, jury rules
item.description: Neglect contributed to the death of a five-month-old girl who died from meningitis after opportunities were missed in hospital to save or prolong her life, an inquest jury has found.

item.title: Exiled critic of Rwandan President Kagame found beheaded in Uganda
item.description: Robert Kabera, a former Rwandan soldier living in Uganda, where he had become a vocal critic of his government back home, was found decapitated near Kampala. Rwandan authorities have been accused of assassinating opponents of President Paul Kagame. FRANCE 24's Aurore Bayoud reports from Kigali, Rwanda.

item.title: Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso resume dialogue with ECOWAS regional bloc
item.description: Three junta-ruled Sahel states – Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso – on Saturday resumed dialogue with the ECOWAS regional bloc, which they withdrew from more than 18 months ago. They agreed to work towards a “framework agreement” on cooperation. FRANCE 24’s regional correspondent Harold Girard tells us more.

item.title: Four soldiers from UN-backed force missing after gang attack in Haiti
item.description: Four soldiers from El Salvador are unaccounted for after being attacked by heavily-armed gangs in Haiti.

item.title: About 6 in 10 Americans confident election will be conducted fairly, accurately: Poll
item.description: Most Americans are not confident Trump will accept midterm results if GOP loses.

item.title: Triumphal Arch final plans submitted to National Capital Planning Commission
item.description: The plans are scheduled to be reviewed at a Nov. 5 National Capital Planning Commission meeting.

item.title: What if an AI bubble bursts — and that accelerates AI job losses?
item.description: Research on past recessions suggests downturns can accelerate automation. That raises the specter of a double whammy for workers.

item.title: WATCH: Study shows Gulf oil spill's lasting damage
item.description: More than 16 years after the BP oil spill off the Gulf Coast, new research reveals lasting damage to marine life.

item.title: Albanians set fire to government buildings and clash with riot police in latest protests
item.description: Demonstrators in Albania have set fire to government buildings and banks, smashed shop windows during the latest clashes with police as they demand the prime minister's resignation.

item.title: TikTok staff raised child safety alarms. Court records show executives failed to act
item.description: The warnings surfaced in a trove of unreported court records. "I have been fighting about fixing this for months with people who didn't think the harms are severe enough," wrote one executive.

item.title: WATCH: Trump announces fuel relief for farmers
item.description: President Donald Trump took his midterm pitch to Kansas Monday night, announcing a new fuel relief program for farmers facing record-high diesel prices.

item.title: Oil-rich Alberta votes to remain part of Canada in historic referendum
item.description: Alberta ‌has voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation.

item.title: Rays will face Brewers in World Series to produce a first-time champion
item.description: The Rays will face the NL champion Milwaukee Brewers in the first matchup in which both teams are seeking their first World Series title since 1980.

item.title: Alberta voters reject a move toward independence in referendum backing Canadian unity
item.description: Voters in Canada's oil-rich Alberta province overwhelmingly backed remaining in Canada, with early referendum results Tuesday delivering a boost to Prime Minister Carney's push for national unity.

item.title: Trump admin sees escalating risk from Houthis, prompting wave of warnings
item.description: The heightened concern comes as Saudi Arabia has struggled to defend against deadly missile and drone strikes on energy and aviation targets.

item.title: Trump's approval rating hits new record low as US midterms loom
item.description: Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low - indicating that next month's midterm elections could be punishing for the Republicans.

item.title: JD Vance says he thinks Trump would endorse him if he ran for president
item.description: Vance added that he hasn't spoken to Trump about it and cautioned that Trump has sometimes let a race play out to see what happens.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir reports on the beloved barn owls that have made Manhattan home
item.description: An expert says it’s the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history.

item.title: WATCH: Teen on how he turned 3D printing idea into a profitable business
item.description: Just three months after graduating high school, Mike Satterlee began using his 3D printer to make hard-shell insulated drink koozies he calls "can coolers."

item.title: Japan launches mission to Mars to bring back samples from its moon
item.description: Japan launched a spacecraft towards Mars in a ground-breaking mission to bring back samples from the largest of the planet's two moons.

item.title: WATCH: Is using cash for purchases becoming a thing of the past?
item.description: Lawmakers on Capitol Hill are considering bills to keep cash an option in commerce.

item.title: Object thought to be Amelia Earhart’s missing plane likely just 'large trees', researchers find
item.description: An expedition to investigate if an anomaly seen on a satellite image of a remote island in the South Pacific was Amelia Earhart’s missing plane has ended without recovering the wreckage.

item.title: UEFA writes to FIFA demanding answers on Trump-Infantino dealings
item.description: European football chiefs have sent a list of 42 questions to FIFA, demanding answers about Gianni Infantino's alleged "conflicts of interest" over business dealings with the Trump family and the World Cup sell-off attempt.

item.title: Doomsday cult leader found guilty of murdering 190 children and one adult
item.description: Doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie, his wife Rhoda Maweu, and 29 other co-accused have been found guilty of the murder of 190 children and one adult.

item.title: WATCH: Blind student, guide dog enjoy adventures in Scotland
item.description: ABC News' Danny New interviews a blind college student in Virginia who's traveling with her guide dog Beasley as she continues her education in Scotland.

item.title: Dems lead GOP in House vote choice as Trump's approval rating hits record low: Poll
item.description: Half or more Americans call every household purchase category measured "unaffordable."

item.title: WATCH: David's Bridal puppy collection
item.description: Wedding retailer David’s Bridal is unveiling its new Puppy Love collection, revealing what the best-dressed best friend will wear at a pet parent’s wedding.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities: Fatal alligator attack in Winter Garden, Florida
item.description: Police say the man was fishing along the shoreline at a park when he was attacked and killed by an alligator.

item.title: WATCH: Hero who stopped Oregon elementary school shooting suspect identified
item.description: ABC News contributor Don Mihalek discusses the bystander credited with stopping the suspected gunman and ongoing investigations.

item.title: WATCH: Nat Geo's 'Moment on the Earth' spotlights the wonders of elephants
item.description: National Geographic shares a closer look at elephants, including how they can eat up to 18 hours a day and even use their trunks to "hug." "Secrets of the Elephants" is streaming now.

item.title: WATCH: Elon Musk unveils Tesla's new Roadster, and it can fly
item.description: Using SpaceX rocket technology, the sports car climbed a curved ramp and hurled itself to a controlled landing.
